title: Entropy-fingerprinter micropolicy for request-level kernel selection
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Summary: Implement a lightweight, per-request fingerprint ("entropy fingerprinter") that summarizes request characteristics and drives a micropolicy to pick the most appropriate kernel variant at runtime. The fingerprint will capture signal dimensions that matter to kernel performance while keeping compute and memory overhead minimal (<= 1% tail latency, <= 2% CPU).

Motivation: Existing runtime heuristics rely on coarse dispatch (arch + flat sequence-length buckets) which misses single-request patterns and transient load shifts that affect tail latency. By computing a compact entropy-based fingerprint (distributional measures, token-type heuristics, effective-seq-estimate, and KV-cache hit hints) we can route specific requests to kernels that minimize latency or cost depending on SLO. This is especially useful for mixed workloads (short, long, chat-prefill mixes) and on heterogeneous fleets.

Design proposal:
- Fingerprint composition: 64-bit hash + three small scalar features: estimated active sequence-length, prefill_vs_decode_prob (0..1), and attention-sparsity-proxy (0..1). The hash aggregates low-cardinality categorical features (model family variant, tokenization bucket, request template id).
- Entropy score: compute a lightweight entropy estimator over the token-type histogram sampled from the first 8 tokens for prefill requests. This single scalar captures distributional skew that predicts attention memory locality.
- Micropolicy: map (arch, gpu-memory-class, fingerprint) -> kernel candidate set using a learned lookup table populated from offline black-box tuning logs and online microbenchmarks. The micropolicy is hierarchical: first rule filters by arch/memory then uses fingerprint distance to known profiles with a small exploration budget (epsilon = 0.02) to allow online discovery.
- Safety: a latency guard rails subsystem ensures kernel picks cannot violate per-request tail SLOs; fallback path to safe kernel on slow warmups or if KV-cache pressure is high.
- Overhead target: fingerprint compute should add <0.2ms median, micropolicy lookup <0.3ms.

Acceptance criteria:
- End-to-end perf: median latency improvement >= 5% and p99 improvement >= 8% on mixed test harness (50% short, 30% chat-prefill, 20% long sequences) vs baseline on heterogeneous cluster.
- Overhead: fingerprint + lookup overhead < 1% median latency and < 3% p99 overhead compared to baseline without selection.
- Safety: no regressions on 10 customer workloads used in closed beta (regression check pipeline required).
- Observability: per-request fingerprint, chosen kernel id, reason code, and fallback events must be emitted to tracing and accessible in Console.

Implementation plan:
1) Prototype fingerprint generator in C++ runtime (feature-flagged) + unit tests (ENG branch).
2) Export microbench harness to collect kernel perf per fingerprint cluster using existing microprobe infra.
3) Offline model: simple k-NN / nearest-profile lookup with LRU cache for hot fingerprints; store as small protobuf persisted in config store.
4) Online exploration: controlled epsilon-greedy sampler per worker with exponential backoff.
5) Metrics and rollback: add new metrics (fingerprint_hit_rate, fingerprint_explore_rate, fingerprint_fallback_count). Expose live dashboard in Console.

Tasks checklist:
- [x] Design doc and simulation (doc: /confluence/runtime/entropy-fingerprint)
- [x] Microbench harness extension (internal PR: github.com/redwood/inference/pull/8261)
- [ ] C++ runtime patch (WIP) (PR: TBD)
- [ ] Integration tests with prefill/decode scheduler test harness
- [ ] Add tracing fields + Console dashboard
- [ ] Beta rollout to dedicated pool alpha-group

Risks & tradeoffs:
- Fingerprint dimensionality: too many features increases memory & lookup surface; too few reduces selectivity. We'll start with minimal set and iterate.
- Overfitting: offline profiles can overfit to microbench noise; we mitigate with online exploration and half-life decay for profile weights.
- Security/PII: fingerprints must not include user text; sampling limited to token-type categories and counts only.

Rollout plan:
- Canary: enable in canary cluster with explore-only mode (no kernel switch) for 1 week to collect distribution.
- Alpha: enable controlled kernel switching in a single Dedicated pool with 5% traffic.
- Beta: expand to multiple pools after 2 weeks of stability and no regressions.
- GA: after 6 weeks of beta with positive perf gains.

Notes on compatibility: Works with current kernel plug-in API. Requires minor schema bump for the kernel-catalog mapping file (manifest v2).
comments: 2025-01-15: Kickoff sync. Agreed on minimal fingerprint (64-bit hash + 3 scalars). Diego to prototype hash function and Ava to update microbench harness.

2025-01-20: PR #8261 adds probe harness changes. Microbench now accepts synthetic fingerprints. Initial runs suggest 6% median gains on a mixed toy workload when routing short chat-prefill to a low-latency kernel.
2025-01-27: Design review notes from Tony (platform): instrument fallback metrics before any rollouts. Added metric names and sampling plan in description.
2025-02-02: Architecture review: we need a small on-disk cache eviction policy to bound memory on workers. Decision: use LRU with 2k entry cap per worker and periodic compaction.

2025-02-03: Diego uploaded prototype branch (feature/entropy-fp) with unit tests and a microperf harness script. Observed 0.15ms median overhead on x86 worker in local run. Next: integrate tracing fields.
